title: Sample idea: a weekly KPI digest for leadership
idea: Send leadership an automatic weekly email with every KPI from every department.

rounds.name: Opening positions
notes: Leaders spend Monday chasing numbers. One digest saves that.
Every KPI from every team is a phone book nobody reads. I think it should be five numbers and one sentence each.
Numbers without their definitions start arguments. Which revenue figure, booked or billed?
Each number needs an owner who answers for it.
Make it live: a dashboard that updates every hour.
rounds.card: A weekly digest with the top KPIs, each with an owner and a definition.

rounds.name: Pushback and concessions
notes: Fine, weekly email beats a dashboard nobody opens. Drop the live version.
Five numbers hide cause and effect. Show what moved and why next to each.
Agreed, but one line of why, not a paragraph.
Flag only numbers outside their normal range so attention goes where it's needed.
If it goes only to leadership, the teams doing the work never see their own numbers.
rounds.card: A weekly digest of eight KPIs with owner, definition, one line of why, and red flags for numbers outside normal range.
credits: red flags for numbers outside normal range

rounds.name: Best version
notes: Send the same digest to team leads too. Costs nothing extra.
Pull from the source systems, not spreadsheets, or the numbers drift.
Short, owned and honest. That's a digest worth opening.
rounds.card: A weekly digest to leadership and team leads: eight KPIs pulled from source systems, each with owner, definition, one line of why and an out-of-range flag.

gates.finding: Two KPIs have no system source today.
gates.change: Start with six automatable KPIs, add two later.

final: Every Monday, leadership and team leads get one digest of six KPIs pulled straight from source systems, growing to eight. Each number has an owner, a definition and one line on why it moved, and anything outside its normal range is flagged first.
changed: Eight KPIs instead of all of them
One line of why per number
dissent: The Inventor still thinks a weekly email is too slow and wants a live view later.
final_credits: one line on why it moved
anything outside its normal range is flagged first
